h: Plan a Day of Wings, Scales and Fresh Air
p: The butterfly house is a lovely place to start, particularly on a cooler morning, when stepping into the tropical warmth feels like a treat. Move slowly and keep still for a bit, and you might find a butterfly settling on your sleeve, much to the kids' delight. Brighter, sunnier days usually mean the butterflies are more active and flying about.

After the warmth, head outside to see the birds of prey and farm animals, then catch an animal talk or handling session if one's on. These hands-on moments are often what kids remember most, and they're a great chance to learn some surprising facts about creatures that might look a bit scary at first.

Wear layers so you can cope with the jump between the humid indoor areas and the outdoor space, and bring a picnic if you fancy, though there's usually a café on site too. With plenty of outdoor space, it's worth checking the forecast and choosing a reasonably dry day if you can.

This part of South Yorkshire has some great extras. Roche Abbey, the ruins of a Cistercian monastery in a beautiful wooded valley, is just a short drive away and is an English Heritage site. Clumber Park, run by the National Trust near Worksop, has huge parkland, a lake and miles of cycle paths. And Creswell Crags, a limestone gorge with caves that were home to Ice Age people, is a fascinating day out with prehistoric cave art. Back in Sheffield itself, the Winter Garden is a huge glasshouse right in the city centre, home to plants from around the world.
